chunks: And from him, from al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who did not know whether he had performed tawaf with six [circuits] or seven, he said: 'He completes it by adding one more [to make it seven].'

key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ: he completes/fulfills (by adding the missing part)

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I am unsure whether I did 6 or 7 rounds of Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in ritual purity, ruling that one defaults to the lower number of completed circuits when in doubt. Consequently, the worshipper performs one additional circuit to bridge the gap, ensuring the obligatory seven are fulfilled without invalidating the act. This reflects the Shia juristic preference for caution in worship while avoiding unnecessary burden, a key nuance in the jurisprudence of Hajj.
